page: Microsoft Azure D16ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock frequency of 3.525 GHz, providing 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. System memory totals 64.0 GB, maintaining an even 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution. The instance includes 644 GB of local SSD storage, while discrete GPU hardware is not present.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core execution ranking in the top 25% of evaluated systems. General multi-core processing, PassMark CPU benchmarks, and Clang compilation tasks align within median ranges. Static web serving throughput and Redis operations show stable middle-tier performance. A measured architectural tradeoff is uncached large-block memory bandwidth, where 256 MB read throughput (39.01 GB/sec) and write throughput (22.73 GB/sec) place in the bottom 25%, despite normal cached small-block bandwidth.

The combination of dedicated AMD EPYC compute cores, 64.0 GB of memory, and integrated local SSD capacity provides consistent qualitative resource efficiency for standard business services without the infrastructure overhead of accelerators. The hardware configuration aligns effectively with relational database servers, Redis memory caches, continuous integration build nodes, and general enterprise web application hosting.
description: The Microsoft Azure D16ads_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AMD EPYC 7763 processor using the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores running at 3.525 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of system memory to maintain a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 644 GB SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted. Benchmark results show strong single-core performance in stress-ng and small-model token generation, balanced by median results across Geekbench and PassMark multi-core workloads. However, uncached memory bandwidth across large data blocks remains in the lower quartile. With its integrated local SSD and balanced compute-to-memory profile, the D16ads_v5 offers reliable operational efficiency for enterprise web serving, Redis caching, CI/CD build environments, and transactional database workloads.
